stem: A trained Massachusetts pharmacist has a patient-specific prescription for one dose of Vivitrol for substance use disorder, the product is supplied in its single-dose presentation, and the prescriber directs pharmacy administration. What is the best legal characterization?

choices.text: This can fit the Massachusetts MH/SUD pharmacist-administration pathway when the remaining guidance requirements are met.
Vivitrol can never be administered by a pharmacist because it treats substance use disorder.
The pharmacist may administer any quantity from non-patient-specific bulk stock without a prescription.
The product becomes Schedule II when administered in a pharmacy.
Only a pharmacy technician may administer this product in Massachusetts.

explanation.core_reasoning: Patient-specific, prescribed single-dose Vivitrol can fit Massachusetts pharmacist administration for SUD when all guidance conditions are met.

choice_analysis.A: Vivitrol is an eligible product under those conditions.
choice_analysis.B: It is expressly listed for this pathway.
choice_analysis.C: The pathway is patient-specific and prescribed.
choice_analysis.D: Administration location does not reclassify naltrexone.
choice_analysis.E: The pathway is for pharmacists/pharmacy interns, not technicians.

related_facts: Prescriber reassessment responsibilities remain part of the treatment relationship.
explanation.mpje_trap: Assuming a medication used for SUD cannot be pharmacy-administered.

reasoning_steps: Identify Vivitrol as listed SUD medication
Confirm patient-specific single-dose and prescriber direction
